description: Alaska Native Villages Work to Enhance Local Economies as They Minimize Environmental Risks is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management | Alaska Outer Continental Shelf Region; U.S. Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement; Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation, Division of Spill Prevention and Response. As reduced sea ice conditions bring increased shipping and development opportunities to the Arctic, Alaska Native Village Corporations are at the table with resource developers, representing the interests of their people and land. Coverage: Alaska (2015). The toolkit gives Alaska as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Rapid warming in the Arctic is reducing the extent of annual sea ice, especially during the long days of summer. The change to more open water can have negative impacts on traditional hunting practices and ice-adapted marine ecosystems, but the receding ice also increases access for ships and creates new opportunities for offshore development.
